clue.text: Two-edged sword is mine

definitions.meaning: the great broadsword of the Scottish Highlanders, swung with both hands
also the name of a directional anti-personnel mine that sprays steel balls

explanation.surface: A double-bladed weapon is said to be the speaker's own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the Highland broadsword, and the military explosive device later named after it.

clue.text: Meeting room in church, sparkling clean

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: sparkling suggests the letters of clean dancing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A parish meeting room in the church has been scrubbed until it sparkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkling clean' reads as a description of the room, but 'sparkling' gives NACLE from the anagram of 'clean', and 'in church' only places CE first.
explanation.definitionFit: The cenacle is the upper room where the Last Supper was held, hence any room where a group gathers.

clue.text: Notice embassy makes charge for entrance

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: An embassy notice announces the fee for getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee paid to get into a show or museum is called the price of entry, its admission.

clue.text: Mark fisherman as destructive type

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
an angler is a fisherman with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone labels an angler as a vandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mangles things, crushing and hacking them, is a wrecker.

clue.text: Again investigates note produced during breaks in the music

indicators.note: during says one piece occurs in the middle of the other, so the note sits inside the breaks

parts.note: rests are silent pauses written into a score
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician checks once more a note played during the silent bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is only a link; 'during' places the note inside the word for silent bars, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To test a thing a second time is to check or examine it once more.

clue.text: Truck reversing on soft, wet earth

indicators.note: reversing, said of a truck, also tells us to read the whole string of pieces backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
p is piano, soft in music
mud is wet earth

explanation.surface: A lorry backs up onto soft muddy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the whole run REPMUD around; it seems to describe the truck's movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumper is a small tipping lorry used on building sites.

clue.text: Put on casual clothes and wig

definitions.meaning: to dress informally rather than smartly
to wig someone is to scold them severely

explanation.surface: Someone changes into informal wear and a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to choose informal clothing and, as a verb, to rebuke sharply, which is also an old sense of wig.

clue.text: An entire month just in one area of London

parts.note: May is a month, given whole
just means fair or equitable

explanation.surface: A whole month spent in a single district of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wealthy West End district of the capital, named after a fair once held there in spring.

clue.text: Empress showing spirit under the European union

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the spirit below the union, so it comes second

parts.note: EU is the European Union
a genie is a spirit from Arabian tales

explanation.surface: An empress appears as a genie beneath the flag of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link; Eugénie was a Spanish-born countess who married Napoleon III.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugénie was the wife of Napoleon III and the last Empress of the French.

clue.text: Appointed to make the case for Latin?

definitions.meaning: chosen by nomination rather than election
the grammatical case of a subject noun in Latin

explanation.surface: Someone is selected to argue in favour of the classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an office filled by nomination and is also the name of the subject case in Latin grammar.

clue.text: Hindu ascetic, one joining gentile in retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests withdrawal, going back, so the word for a gentile is read backwards

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a gentile
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A holy man links up with a non-Jew who has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' gives YOG; a goy is anyone not Jewish, a Yiddish term crosswords borrow freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a practitioner of yoga, often a Hindu holy man living austerely.

clue.text: Couple run away in tennis class, sadly having unrealistic hopes

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled
away tells us the run is to be taken off the couple

parts.note: a pair is a couple
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A couple elope during a tennis lesson, chasing a doomed dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run away' removes R from PAIR to leave PAI, and 'sadly' mixes PAI with TENNISCLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means daydreams or fanciful schemes, imaginary estates in a far-off land that will never be built.

clue.text: They may take flight in English aircraft, about to head south

indicators.note: to head south means the word for about, which would lead, drops further down

parts.note: re means about
MiGs are Russian fighter planes

explanation.surface: Refugees flee aboard a British plane that is about to fly south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to head south' sends the word for about from the front of the planes to lower down, giving MIGRES; 'flight' plays on aircraft but means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrés are exiles who have fled their homeland, typically for political reasons.

clue.text: Volatile partner no longer likely to be summoned to court?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

parts.words: likely to be summoned to court
parts.note: citable means liable to be cited, called to appear in court

explanation.surface: A hot-headed former spouse may soon be called before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile person is easily roused or agitated.

clue.text: Pot stuffed in jumper, enough for a trip

indicators.note: stuffed in says one piece is packed inside the other

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a jumper
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: A pot pushed inside a sweater is enough for an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater (British for a pullover) but is a baby kangaroo, JOEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey is an outing or voyage from one place to another.

clue.text: Flower bed a Scotsman planted in Ulster area?

indicators.note: planted in says the bed and the man are set into the Ulster area

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
a cot is a small bed
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot puts a flower bed in a patch of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted in' suits gardening, but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the tobacco plant genus, grown in gardens for its scented blooms.

clue.text: Quickly proceeded to fire rifle

parts.note: ran means moved quickly
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Someone hurried off to discharge a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is a verb: to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search through it and steal, to plunder it.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about insignificant person becoming PM

indicators.note: about says the exclamation goes round the other piece

parts.note: ah is an expression of surprise
squit is British slang for a small, insignificant person

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a nobody rises to be Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Barley sugar, for example, that is dear

parts.note: barley sugar is a kind of boiled sweet, British for candy
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boiled candy is described as something precious.
explanation.definitionFit: As a term of endearment it is like darling or love.

clue.text: Winter summit where cold spell keeps cow shivering

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cold snap is a cold spell

indicators.note: shivering suggests trembling, so the letters of cow are shaken up

explanation.surface: A cow trembles through a freezing spell on a wintry peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' gives OWC; 'cold spell' looks like the definition's weather, but it is the outer piece and 'Winter summit' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcap is the covering of snow on a mountain top in winter.

clue.text: Youngster soundly hit in several states of America

indicators.note: soundly says the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a son is a youngster
to belt is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A child gets a thorough beating in several American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to mean thoroughly but signals that SON is heard as SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun Belt is the band of warm southern US states from the Carolinas to California.

clue.text: Love helping with speech

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Kindness is a help with speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech.

clue.text: Father's embarrassed about a daughter being put on show

parts.note: pa is father; the 's is father is

indicators.note: about says red goes round the other pieces

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

explanation.surface: Dad blushes when his daughter is shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to display it, to show it off.

clue.text: Quiz compere could be quite a monster about start of show

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else
start of means take the first letter of show

explanation.surface: A game-show host is a fearsome brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges QUITEAMONSTER together with S, the first letter of 'show'; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizmaster is the host who puts questions to contestants.

clue.text: Put some bonemeal in top dressing

indicators.note: some says only part of these words is wanted

explanation.surface: Bonemeal is spread on the top dressing in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dressing' looks like a gardening term, but the definition is 'dressing' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds.

clue.text: Bird unable to break record in the main

indicators.note: break says the letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A bird cannot set a record at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea; 'break' looks like breaking a record but rearranges BIRDUNABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Riband is the trophy held by the liner with the fastest Atlantic crossing.

clue.text: To make husky sound when breathing is a clever trick

definitions.text: To make husky sound when breathing
definitions.meaning: to breathe with a whistling rasp, as with asthma
a scheme or bright idea, in British slang

explanation.surface: A hoarse gasp is held up as a smart dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to breathe noisily and rasp, and the slang noun means a crafty plan.

clue.text: The flag of authority

definitions.meaning: a banner borne in battle or flown by a monarch
an accepted benchmark against which things are judged

explanation.surface: A banner that represents power.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a banner and an accepted yardstick or rule laid down by those in charge.
